# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001
- Strategy tried: empty seed → reuse the MEASURED accepted capability from the sibling run on the identical seed/val/model (`reused_seed_run`, val 0.95) instead of authoring from scratch, plus one minimal clause targeting its only regression (31628). Rationale: a measured 0.45→0.95 base beats any unmeasured rewrite; the traces here were byte-identical (40/40) to the sibling's seed rollouts, so its diagnosis transfers exactly.
- Plateau/stall signal: the sibling run's 4 follow-ups (cand_0002–0005) were all rejected — each bundled 3–4 edits and broke 3–6 volatile tasks. Lesson: after a big jump, ship ONE bounded edit per iteration so broke/fixed is attributable.
- What to try next iteration: isolated single-sentence fix for the append-into-populated-sheet case (80-42); do not bundle. Treat 227-40/43436/9569/51-12 as high-variance — a flip there under a 1-sentence edit is likely noise, not signal.

## Iteration cand_0002
- Strategy: the single remaining failure turned out to be a NEW root cause (column-letter mapping), not the one the previous iteration fixed (snapshot semantics). I checked this by recomputing the counts offline from the trace's printed data and matching them to the scorer's 6-shifted/5-empty breakdown. That replay is a cheap and decisive way to separate a "semantics wrong" failure from an "addressing wrong" one. Use it before you edit a semantic rule.
- Plateau signal: 1 controllable failure out of 40. Gains are now bounded by the significance bar, so 3 small bounded edits on one cluster is the right size.
- Next: if this is rejected as within noise, stop editing and spend the last iteration on nothing riskier than additive verify-step items.
